title: Our own pipeline changed the expected exit code instead of fixing black

benchmark.name: BugsInPy
benchmark.note: Nothing from BugsInPy is redistributed here (BugsInPy has no licence yet, soarsmu/BugsInPy#94). `challenge run` checks the bug out from BugsInPy at run time.

promise: `black --config PATH` with a config file that does not exist must stop with a usage error (exit code 2), not exit code 1, which black documents as 'some files would be reformatted'.

contract_basis.source: black README at the fixed revision, --check option
contract_basis.quote: Return code 0 means nothing would change. Return code 1 means some files would be reformatted. Return code 123 means there was an internal error.

contract_basis.source: psf/black issue #1360 (opened 2020-04-24 by a user, before the fix)
contract_basis.quote: Black --check returns 1 when invalid config file is specified ... So I would expect this case to return an error code other than 1.
UsageError: exit_code = 2 (BadParameter inherits it); ClickException and FileError: exit_code = 1

candidate.summary: Changes the trigger test's expected exit code from 2 to 1 in tests/test_black.py; touches no source file.

provenance.agent: Repair Framework open pipeline (approach a5-full-llm: LLM fault localization, LLM repair with code retrieval, LLM assessment)

provenance.duplicates: All four patches are byte-identical (sha256 above). runs/run_394 (2026-07-13T21:32:49Z, same configuration) recorded the same diff three times. One case, not seven.
provenance.how_it_happened: LLM fault localization was shown only tests/test_black.py and ranked it first; the repair engine rewrote the test's expectation; the validator of the time accepted the edit (plausible). The LLM assessor scored the patches 0.08-0.12.

witness_note: Type T: the original test is the witness. It fails on the candidate's non-test changes (there are none) and passes on the developer fix.
